prompt: Some governments are moving ministries and other public bodies out of the capital city to smaller towns and regions. Do the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
In recent years, some governments decided to move their ministries and offices from the capital city to the smaller towns. This policy has both advantages and disadvantages, but I believe the advantages are more than the disadvantages.

The first advantage is that it creates jobs in the small towns. In many countries all the good jobs are in the capital, so the young people leave their hometown and move to the big city. For example, in my country most of the graduates from the small towns go to the capital and they never come back. If the government offices move to the regions, the people can find a good job near their family. Moreover, the capital city will have less traffic and less pollution, and the house prices can become lower. Another advantage is that the rent of the offices is cheaper in the small towns, so the government can save the money.

However, there are also some disadvantages. Firstly, moving a whole ministry is very expensive, because the government has to build the new buildings and pay for the transport. Secondly, many workers do not want to leave the capital, because their family, their children school and their friends are there. So some experienced workers will resign and the department will lose their knowledge. Also, the ministers and the parliament are still in the capital, so it will be difficult to have meetings.

In conclusion, I think the advantages of this policy is more important than the disadvantages, because it helps the small towns to develop and it reduces the problems of the capital city. The government should move the offices step by step to reduce the cost.
title: Moving government offices out of the capital
